Remove pan from oven.
Stir in butter, crispy bacon chunks, and half the gremolata.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately with the remaining gremolata sprinkled on top.
notes: Steaming the vegetables dry after parboiling ensures a crispier exterior during roasting.
Do not crowd the roasting pan to allow for even browning.
Use a waxy potato variety to ensure the cubes maintain their shape during roasting and tossing.

recipes.recipe_name: Chinese Tomato and Egg Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow, white porcelain rimmed bowl, showcasing a vibrant contrast between glossy, bright red tomato wedges and large, fluffy clouds of golden-yellow scrambled eggs. The tomatoes are cut into uniform wedges, softened into a thick, shimmering savory-sweet sauce that coats every element. Scattered across the top are bright green, bias-cut scallion rounds. The arrangement is natural and fluid, filling the center of the bowl with moderate negative space around the rim. The setting features a dark wood table, a pair of polished dark wood chopsticks on a ceramic holder, and a small side bowl of steamed jasmine rice. Natural side-lighting highlights the silky texture of the eggs and the reflective glaze of the tomato sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed long-grain jasmine rice
Accompany with a side of quickly blanched bok choy
Provide chopsticks and a short-handled ceramic soup spoon

ingredients.name: Ripe Roma tomatoes, cut into 8 wedges each
Scallions, white and green parts separated and sliced

instructions: Whisk eggs with Shaoxing wine and salt until well combined.
Heat 30ml oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering.
Pour in eggs. Stir gently until puffed and just set. Remove eggs immediately.
Add remaining oil to the wok. Sauté ginger, garlic, and scallion whites for 30 seconds.
Add tomato wedges. Stir-fry until skins begin to soften and juices release.
Stir in soy sauce and sugar. Simmer for 1 minute.
Pour in cornstarch slurry. Stir until sauce thickens and becomes glossy.
Return eggs to the wok. Fold gently to combine without breaking the egg clouds.
Drizzle with sesame oil. Garnish with scallion greens.
Serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.
notes: Use very ripe tomatoes for maximum juice and flavor.
Do not overcook the eggs in the first step; they should remain soft and custardy.
Adjust sugar based on the natural acidity of the tomatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Roasted Chicken with Morel Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single, golden-brown pan-roasted chicken thigh placed off-center on a large, white porcelain plate. The skin is crispy and deeply caramelized. A generous portion of whole and halved morel mushrooms is nestled beside the chicken, coated in a glossy, pale-ivory cream sauce. The sauce pools naturally around the base of the chicken without covering the crispy skin. Vibrant green chopped parsley and a small sprig of fresh thyme are scattered over the morels. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark oak table. A silver fork and knife lie on a folded white cotton napkin. Natural light from a window illuminates the textures of the pitted mushrooms and the glistening sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty French baguette to soak up the sauce
Pair with a glass of chilled Chardonnay or Pinot Noir
Traditional bistro-style service with simple silver flatware
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the skillet.
Sear for 6 minutes until skin is golden and crispy.
Flip chicken and cook for 4 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Clean morels with a soft brush. Leave small ones whole. Halve large ones lengthwise.
Drain excess fat from skillet. Melt 15g butter.
Add morels to skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until browned.
Add shallots and garlic. Cook for 2 minutes until translucent.
Deglaze pan with white wine. Scrape browned bits from the bottom.
Reduce wine by half.
Add chicken stock and thyme sprigs. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer for 3 minutes until sauce thickens.
Whisk in remaining 15g butter to finish the sauce.
Return chicken to the pan briefly to coat.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Clean morels carefully as they can trap grit in their crevices
Do not crowd the pan when searing chicken to ensure crispy skin
Use a meat thermometer to confirm chicken reaches exactly 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Lomo Saltado
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lomo Saltado presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features 3cm chunks of seared beef sirloin with a deep brown crust. These are mixed with thick, glossy wedges of purple red onion and bright red Roma tomatoes. Golden, thick-cut potato batons are scattered through the beef mixture, all coated in a dark, shimmering sauce. A neat, molded dome of fluffy white rice sits on the side of the plate. Fresh green cilantro leaves garnish the top. The scene is set on a light wooden bistro table with a white cotton napkin and a small side bowl of spicy green aji sauce. The lighting is natural and even.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Aji Verde (green chili sauce)
Accompany with Inca Kola or a glass of red wine
Traditionally eaten with both rice and potatoes in the same meal

ingredients.name: Red onions, cut into thick wedges
Roma tomatoes, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Sear beef in batches until browned and medium-rare.
Remove beef from wok and set aside.
Add remaining oil to the wok.
Stir-fry onion wedges for 2 minutes until slightly charred but crisp.
Add garlic and aji amarillo paste. Stir for 30 seconds.
Return beef to the wok.
Pour in soy sauce and red wine vinegar. Toss quickly.
Add tomato wedges. Stir for 30 seconds to warm through.
Fold in the cooked potato fries and half the cilantro.
Remove from heat immediately.
Serve with white rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding beef to achieve a smoky flavor.
Do not overcook the tomatoes; they should be warm but hold their shape.
The potatoes should be added at the very last second to maintain some crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Pibil with Pickled Red Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo Pibil served on a matte white ceramic plate. A vibrant green banana leaf lines the plate, cradling two whole, bone-in chicken thighs. The chicken is coated in a deep, earthy red achiote sauce with a glossy finish. A mound of bright pink pickled red onion slivers sits atop the chicken. Small sprigs of fresh cilantro and a single charred habanero chili provide color contrast. Beside the chicken lie three warm, hand-pressed corn tortillas folded into triangles. The setting is a rustic wooden table with a linen napkin. Natural side-lighting highlights the succulent texture of the meat and the delicate grain of the tortillas.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Accompany with black beans and rice
Provide extra habanero salsa for heat

ingredients.name: Bitter orange juice (or 100ml orange/100ml lime mix)

instructions: Whisk achiote paste, citrus juice, garlic, oregano, and cumin until smooth.
Pour marinade over chicken thighs. Refrigerate for 4 hours.
Boil vinegar with 5g salt. Pour over sliced red onions. Let sit 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 180°C.
Line a baking dish with banana leaves. Overlap leaves to cover bottom and sides.
Place chicken and marinade inside. Fold leaves over chicken to seal tightly.
Cover dish with foil. Bake for 45 minutes.
Remove foil and open leaves. Bake 15 more minutes until chicken reaches 75°C.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Softening banana leaves over a gas flame makes them pliable.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Wild Boar with Caraway and Sage
recipes.visual_description: Braised Wild Boar with Caraway and Sage is presented as generous 4cm chunks of tender meat, coated in a glossy, deep mahogany reduction of red wine and apple cider. The meat is arranged centrally in a wide, matte-finish cream porcelain bowl, showing visible textures of the slow-cooked fibers. Whole caraway seeds and flash-fried dark green sage leaves are scattered naturally over the dish. Thick rounds of softened carrots provide pops of orange against the dark sauce. The dish is served on a rustic dark oak table with a side of traditional buttered spaetzle in a small separate ceramic dish. Soft, natural window lighting highlights the moist sheen of the sauce and the earthy textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with buttered spaetzle or rustic rye bread
Pair with a side of braised red cabbage
Serve alongside a dry Riesling or a medium-bodied red wine

ingredients.name: Wild boar shoulder, cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Pat boar chunks dry with paper towels.
Season meat with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear boar chunks in batches until browned on all sides.
Remove meat and set aside.
Add onion and carrots to the same pot.
Sauté for 5 minutes until onions soften.
Add caraway seeds and sage leaves.
Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine and apple cider.
Scrape the bottom of the pot to release browned bits.
Return meat and any juices to the pot.
Add game stock until meat is mostly submerged.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 2 hours.
Remove lid and increase heat slightly.
Reduce sauce for 15 minutes until glossy and thick.
notes: Wild boar is leaner than pork; low and slow braising is essential for tenderness.
Ensure the red wine is dry to prevent the sauce from becoming too sweet.

recipes.recipe_name: Campari-Acai Glazed Chicken with Savory Banana Puree
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a whole, roasted chicken breast coated in a glossy, deep violet acai and Campari glaze. The chicken is centered on a smooth, circular bed of pale cream-colored savory banana and almond paste puree. Toasted green hemp seeds are sprinkled over the chicken. Around the base of the puree, thin, star-shaped cross-sections of bright green bilimbi add vibrant color and sharp contrast. The plating is clean and professional on a matte white ceramic plate, utilizing moderate negative space. The entire plate is visible under natural, even lighting, highlighting the contrast between the dark purple glaze and the light-colored puree. The setting is a modern bistro table with a cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of toasted farofa
Accompany with a crisp Brazilian pilsner or a dry sparkling wine
instructions: Toast hemp seeds in a dry pan over medium heat until golden. Set aside.
Peel and cut bananas into 2cm thick rounds.
Boil banana rounds in salted water for 10 minutes until soft. Drain well.
Blend warm bananas with almond paste and salt until smooth. Keep warm.
Thinly slice 4 bilimbi fruits into star-shaped cross-sections. Mince the remaining 2.
Combine acai pulp, Campari, and minced bilimbi in a small saucepan.
Simmer sauce over medium heat for 8 minutes until reduced by half. Strain through a fine sieve.
Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan. Sear chicken for 4 minutes on each side.
Transfer pan to oven at 180°C. Roast chicken until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Brush chicken heavily with the acai-Campari reduction.
Place a large spoonful of banana puree in the center of each plate.
Place one whole glazed chicken breast on top of the puree.
Garnish with toasted hemp seeds and bilimbi star slices.
notes: Ensure acai pulp is unsweetened to maintain the savory profile.
The almond paste provides fat and body to the banana puree, similar to a traditional mash.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cucumber and Potato Starter with Cured Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion served on a handcrafted cream ceramic plate with a textured, matte finish. The dish features a base of two vibrant green Little Gem lettuce leaves. Arranged naturally on top are 1cm cubes of golden-skinned boiled potatoes and 2cm seared chicken chunks with a light brown crust. Translucent 3mm fermented cucumber rounds and thin pink pickled onion rings provide bright accents. Two quarters of a soft-boiled egg with jammy orange yolks are positioned near the center. Irregular golden-brown bread crumbs are scattered over the arrangement. The plating is minimalist and airy, utilizing negative space. Soft natural light emphasizes the varied textures of the crisp bread and moist chicken.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on handmade stoneware
Accompany with small glasses of chilled aquavit
Use wooden or forged steel utensils
instructions: Rub chicken with 10g salt. Cure for 20 minutes. Rinse and pat dry.
Cut chicken into 2cm cubes. Sear in a pan until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Boil potatoes whole in skins until tender. Cool and cut into 1cm cubes.
Slice cucumber into 3mm rounds. Submerge in brine of 200ml water and 10g salt for 24 hours.
Slice onion into thin rings. Quick-pickle in vinegar for 15 minutes.
Soft-boil eggs for 6.5 minutes. Peel and cut into quarters.
Tear bread into small irregular pieces. Toast in a dry pan until golden and crisp.
Wash and dry lettuce leaves. Use as a base for the salad.
Combine potatoes, cucumbers, and onions. Place on lettuce leaves.
Add chicken chunks and egg quarters. Top with toasted bread crumbs.
notes: Use potato skins to add earthy flavor and reduce waste
Save cucumber fermentation brine for future salad dressings
Ensure bread is completely dry for maximum crunch

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Afritada
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pork Afritada served in a shallow white ceramic bowl on a dark wooden table. The dish features thick 3cm chunks of tender pork shoulder coated in a rich, reddish-orange tomato sauce. Interspersed are soft, golden-browned 3cm potato cubes and vibrant orange 3cm carrot cubes. Small bits of softened onion and tomato skin are visible in the sauce. A sprinkle of cracked black pepper covers the surface. Beside the bowl sits a small mound of steamed white rice. A traditional Filipino spoon and fork lie on a simple woven placemat. The lighting is warm and domestic, suggesting a cozy evening meal. The entire plate is visible, showing a natural, hearty arrangement.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed white jasmine rice.
Offer a small dipping bowl of fish sauce with a crushed bird's eye chili.
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Fry potato and carrot cubes until edges are golden. Remove and set aside.
Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in the same pot until fragrant.
Add pork chunks. Sear until meat is browned on all sides.
Stir in chopped tomatoes. Cook until tomatoes soften and release juices.
Season with fish sauce and black pepper.
Pour in water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 40 minutes until pork is tender.
Add the fried potatoes and carrots back into the pot.
Simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens and vegetables are soft.
notes: Pork shoulder provides the best fat-to-meat ratio for a tender stew.
Cut all vegetables into uniform 3cm cubes to ensure even cooking and traditional appearance.

recipes.recipe_name: Alpine Onion and Apple Cheese Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single individual white porcelain baking dish sits on a rustic light oak table. Inside, golden-brown fried sourdough cubes are layered with soft, dark mahogany caramelized onion strips and pale green apple wedges. A thick layer of melted Gruyère cheese covers the ingredients, showing toasted brown blisters and a glossy, stringy texture. A perfectly round poached egg rests in the center, its white set and opaque. Fresh green thyme leaves and coarse cracked black pepper are scattered over the top. The background features a clean white linen napkin and a heavy silver fork. Natural side lighting highlights the steam rising from the dish and the contrast between the crisp bread and melted cheese.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of cornichons
Pair with a dry white wine from the Savoie region
Present in individual ceramic croûte dishes
instructions: Melt 30g butter in a pan over medium heat.
Add onion strips and a pinch of salt.
Cook onions for 20 minutes until deep brown.
Add apple wedges and thyme to the pan.
Sauté for 5 minutes until apples soften.
In a separate pan, melt remaining butter.
Fry bread cubes until golden and crisp.
Arrange fried bread, onions, and apples in four individual baking dishes.
Pour 60ml stock into each dish.
Top each dish with 50g grated cheese.
Bake at 200°C for 10 minutes until cheese bubbles.
Poach eggs in simmering water for 3 minutes.
Place one poached egg on top of each dish before serving.
notes: Use day-old bread for better texture when frying.
Ensure the onions are deeply caramelized for maximum umami flavor.
Keep the egg yolk runny to create a natural sauce for the bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Cod Tacos with Sharp Cheddar
recipes.visual_description: Two lightly charred flour tortillas hold thick, golden-seared cod chunks. The cod is opaque and flaky. Bright orange melted cheddar cheese drapes over the fish. Vibrant red onion rings and green jalapeno slices are scattered on top. The arrangement is clean and central on a white porcelain plate. A small wedge of lime and a sprig of fresh cilantro provide color contrast. The background is a dark wood bistro table. Natural side lighting highlights the texture of the seared fish and the soft matte surface of the tortillas. A blue cotton napkin sits neatly to the left. The scene is uncluttered and professional. This single portion presentation emphasizes fresh ingredients and balanced proportions.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh lime wedges for acidity
Accompany with a side of salsa verde
Provide pickled radishes as a palate cleanser
instructions: Slice red onion into thin rings.
Slice jalapenos into thin rounds.
Mince the garlic finely.
Grate the cheddar cheese.
Cut cod into 4cm thick chunks.
Season cod with salt, pepper, and minced garlic.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear cod chunks for 3 minutes per side until golden.
Remove fish from pan and set aside.
Wipe pan clean and add remaining oil.
Sauté onions and jalapenos for 2 minutes until softened.
Char tortillas in a dry pan over high heat for 30 seconds per side.
Place two tortillas on each plate.
Distribute cod chunks evenly among tortillas.
Top with grated cheddar and sautéed vegetables.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the cod is patted dry before searing to achieve a better crust.
Remove jalapeno seeds if a milder heat profile is desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Abalone Mushroom and Fish Tofu Udon
recipes.visual_description: Present the dish on a wide, matte white porcelain plate. The udon noodles are glossy and coiled naturally in the center, coated in a light, amber-colored sauce. Thick, meaty chunks of seared abalone mushroom and golden-brown cubes of fish tofu are nestled on top of the noodles. Vibrant green bok choy leaves are tucked to the side. The dish is garnished with finely julienned scallions and a sprinkle of toasted white sesame seeds. Use a modern bistro setting with a dark wood table. Include a pair of dark wood chopsticks resting on a ceramic holder and a small side dish of pickled daikon. Natural side lighting highlights the textures of the mushrooms and the sheen of the noodles.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pickled daikon to cleanse the palate
Accompany with a hot bowl of clear dashi broth
Traditional chopsticks and ceramic noodle bowl presentation
instructions: Boil water in a large pot.
Cook udon noodles for 2 minutes until tender.
Drain noodles and rinse with cold water.
Heat neutral oil in a wok over high heat.
Add abalone mushroom chunks to the wok.
Sear mushrooms for 4 minutes until golden brown.
Add fish tofu cubes and fry for 3 minutes.
Stir in minced ginger, garlic, and doubanjiang.
Cook for 1 minute until aromatic.
Add baby bok choy halves and 30ml of water.
Steam for 2 minutes until the greens wilt.
Add udon noodles and white soy sauce.
Toss for 2 minutes to emulsify the sauce.
Drizzle with sesame oil and remove from heat.
notes: White soy sauce provides saltiness without darkening the udon noodles
Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding mushrooms to achieve a proper sear
The fish tofu should have a slightly bouncy texture after frying

recipes.recipe_name: Kimchi and Lentil Shakshuka
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Kimchi and Lentil Shakshuka presented in a wide, white porcelain bowl. The base features a rich, dark stew of tender lentils and chopped red kimchi, cooked with diced onions and green bell pepper chunks. Two whole poached eggs sit atop the mixture, with firm whites and liquid yolks. Thick dollops of white yogurt and streaks of red hot sauce garnish the top, alongside crumbled white cheese. Two thick, golden-fried bread batons are placed on the rim. A side plate holds a vibrant salad of mixed greens, thin cucumber slices, crisp apple wedges, and wedges of ripe avocado. The arrangement is clean and professional on a rustic wooden table with a linen napkin and a stainless steel spoon.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a shared cast-iron skillet for communal dining
Accompany with toasted sesame seeds and nori strips
Provide chopsticks for the side salad and a spoon for the shakshuka
instructions: Sauté diced onion and bell pepper in oil for 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and lentils.
Add vegetable stock, cola, and chopped kimchi.
Simmer for 20 minutes until lentils are tender.
Add green beans and cook for 3 minutes.
Create four wells in the mixture and crack one egg into each.
Cover and cook until egg whites are set but yolks remain runny.
Fry sourdough bread slices in butter until golden and crisp.
Whisk together yogurt, cream, and hot sauce.
Whisk apricot jam with a splash of vinegar to create a dressing.
Toss salad greens, cucumber, avocado, and apple wedges with the dressing.
Garnish shakshuka with crumbled feta and the spicy yogurt sauce.
notes: The cola adds a subtle sweetness that balances the acidity of the fermented kimchi.
Ensure the lentils are fully submerged during the braise to cook evenly.
Use aged kimchi for a deeper, more savory flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Barramundi with Ginger-Soy Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A whole pan-seared barramundi fillet is the centerpiece, featuring a perfectly crisp, golden-brown skin. It rests on a neat mound of steamed jasmine rice in a clean white porcelain bowl. Two vibrant green bok choy halves, lightly charred from the pan, are positioned alongside the fish. A glossy, dark amber ginger-soy glaze is drizzled over the fillet, highlighting its flaky texture. The dish is garnished with finely sliced green onions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds. The setting includes a minimalist wooden table, a pair of dark bamboo chopsticks, and a small ceramic dish of pickled radishes. Natural, soft light emphasizes the contrast between the dark glaze and white rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pickled daikon or ginger
Provide bamboo chopsticks and a wide ceramic spoon
Accompany with hot jasmine tea
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice until water runs clear.
Cook rice in 600ml water until tender and fluffy.
Whisk soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, ginger, and garlic in a small bowl.
Pat barramundi fillets dry with paper towels.
Season the skin side of the fish with salt.
Heat neutral oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Place fish skin-side down in the pan.
Press firmly with a spatula for 30 seconds to ensure even contact.
Sear for 4 minutes until skin is golden and very crisp.
Flip the fillets carefully.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until the fish is opaque and internal temperature reaches 63°C.
Remove fish from the pan and set aside.
Add halved bok choy to the same pan and sear for 2 minutes.
Pour the soy mixture over the bok choy.
Simmer for 1 minute until the glaze thickens and coats the vegetables.
Serve the whole fillet over rice with the glazed bok choy on the side.
notes: Ensure the pan is very hot before adding the fish to achieve a crispy skin.
Do not move the fish during the first 2 minutes of searing.
Use a fish spatula for easier flipping.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Batang Fish on Bean Puree with Black Currant Relish
recipes.visual_description: Twelve bite-sized canapés arranged casually on a matte white ceramic platter. Each canapé features a base of smooth, pale ivory cannellini bean puree. Resting on the puree is a thick, 3cm cube of pan-seared batang fish with a deep golden-brown crust on all sides. The fish is topped with a small mound of finely diced, light green artichoke hearts and tiny, translucent yellow bits of candied citrus. A vibrant, deep purple black currant reduction is drizzled over the top, creating a sharp color contrast. A single, bright green flat-leaf parsley sprig provides a final garnish. The platter sits on a dark oak wooden table under warm, natural kitchen lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an appetizer on a communal platter.
Accompany with chilled sparkling water or a dry white wine.
Provide small cocktail napkins for finger food service.
instructions: Cut batang fish into 12 equal 3cm cubes.
Season fish cubes with salt and pepper.
Mash cannellini beans with 10ml olive oil and lemon juice until smooth.
Dice artichoke hearts into small 5mm pieces.
Mince candied citrus peel finely.
Mix diced artichokes with minced candied peel in a small bowl.
Simmer black currants with 15ml water in a pan for 5 minutes.
Press currants through a fine mesh sieve to create a thick syrup.
Heat remaining olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Sear fish cubes for 2 minutes per side until golden and opaque.
Place 12 small spoonfuls of bean puree onto a ceramic platter.
Top each puree dollop with one seared fish cube.
Spoon the artichoke mixture over the fish.
Drizzle each piece with the black currant reduction.
Garnish with one small parsley leaf per piece.
notes: Batang fish is also known as Spanish Mackerel.
Ensure the bean puree is thick enough to support the weight of the fish.
Pat the fish dry with paper towels before searing to ensure a crisp crust.

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Beef and Bean Stew
recipes.visual_description: A deep, rustic ceramic bowl holds a thick, vibrant red-orange stew. The focus is on 3cm tender beef chunks and whole, glossy red kidney beans emerging from the rich, paprika-infused gravy. Softened diced tomatoes and translucent onion fragments are visible throughout the liquid. The beef is presented as natural, hearty chunks, never sliced or fanned. The dish is garnished with a small pinch of fresh parsley. It sits on a dark, well-worn wooden kitchen table next to a thick wedge of crusty white bread. A vintage pewter spoon rests on a simple, off-white linen napkin. The lighting is warm and domestic, highlighting the matte texture of the ceramic and the glistening stew. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with thick slices of fresh sourdough or rye bread
Accompany with pickled cucumbers or fermented peppers
Add a dollop of sour cream (Tejföl) for extra richness
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add diced onions and sauté for 8 minutes until translucent.
Add beef cubes and sear until browned on all sides.
Stir in minced garlic and diced tomatoes.
Remove pot from heat and stir in the paprika to prevent burning.
Return to heat and add bay leaves and black pepper.
Pour in water until the meat is just covered.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 90 minutes until beef is tender.
Add drained kidney beans and simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove bay leaves and season with salt before serving.
notes: Ensure the pot is removed from heat when adding paprika to avoid a bitter taste.
Beef chuck is preferred for its fat content and tenderness after long simmering.
If the stew is too thin, simmer uncovered for the final 15 minutes.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom Risotto with Thyme and Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of fluid, creamy risotto is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The rice spreads naturally across the plate, demonstrating a 'wave' consistency rather than a molded shape. Golden-brown sautéed mushroom chunks are scattered across the top. Fresh thyme leaves and thin shavings of Parmesan cheese provide textural contrast. The dish is placed on a light oak bistro table with a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver spoon. Natural side lighting highlights the glossy texture of the starch-rich sauce. Small drops of extra virgin olive oil glisten on the surface, emphasizing the savory, rich finish. The entire plate is visible against a minimal, modern background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while the rice maintains its fluid consistency
Accompany with a glass of dry Italian white wine like Gavi or Pinot Grigio
Place a small bowl of extra grated Parmesan on the table
instructions: Heat vegetable stock in a pot. Keep it at a low simmer.
Sauté quartered mushrooms in olive oil until browned. Remove and set aside.
Sauté diced shallots in the same pan until translucent.
Add Arborio rice. Toast for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in white wine. Stir until liquid evaporates.
Add one ladle of hot stock. Stir rice constantly.
Add more stock once the previous ladle is absorbed.
Repeat process for 18 minutes until rice is al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter and grated parmesan vigorously.
Fold in sautéed mushroom chunks and thyme.
Adjust consistency with a splash of stock to ensure it is fluid. Season with salt and pepper.
notes: Stirring constantly is essential to release the starch for a creamy texture
Do not let the stock boil vigorously; a gentle simmer prevents the rice from breaking
The risotto should flow like lava when the plate is tilted

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Paprikash
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Paprikash served on a heavy, hand-painted ceramic plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are braised to a deep, glossy orange-red color. They rest on a generous bed of small, irregularly shaped nokedli dumplings. A thick, vibrant paprika gravy coats the meat and flows naturally into the dumplings. A clean dollop of cool white sour cream sits on top of the chicken, slightly melting into the warm sauce. Finely chopped green parsley is scattered across the dish. The plate sits on a weathered wooden table with a side bowl of vinegar-brined cucumber salad. Warm, diffused kitchen light emphasizes the rich, creamy texture of the sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with nokedli (Hungarian dumplings) or wide egg noodles
Include a side of mizeria (cucumber salad) or pickled gherkins
Provide crusty rye bread to soak up the paprika sauce
instructions: Season chicken pieces with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add onions to the skillet. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in minced garlic for 1 minute.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in paprika to avoid burning.
Return chicken to the skillet. Pour in chicken stock.
Simmer covered for 30 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Whisk sour cream and flour together in a small bowl.
Temper the cream by adding two spoons of hot cooking liquid to it. Mix well.
Stir the cream mixture back into the skillet. Simmer for 5 minutes until sauce thickens.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Removing the pan from heat before adding paprika prevents bitterness.
Tempering the sour cream prevents it from curdling in the hot sauce.
Always use authentic Hungarian sweet paprika for the best flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Banana and Herb Dutch Baby with Raspberry Gastrique
recipes.visual_description: A single individual-sized, golden-brown Dutch baby pancake is presented in a seasoned 12 cm black cast-iron skillet. The edges are dramatically puffed and crisp, rising high above the rim. The center is custardy, featuring three thick, sautéed banana coins with deep golden caramelization and visible sear marks. A sharp, vibrant raspberry gastrique is drizzled in precise lines across the surface, providing a deep crimson contrast to the yellow batter. Small, fresh thyme leaves are scattered purposefully over the top, adding earthy green flecks. The skillet is centered on a light oak table, accompanied by a folded white linen napkin and a simple silver fork. The arrangement is clean and professional, highlighting the airy textures under bright, natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while puffed
Accompany with a crisp green salad with vinaigrette
Use traditional French silver bistro cutlery
instructions: Place four 12 cm cast-iron skillets in the oven and preheat to 220°C.
Whisk eggs, milk, flour, salt, pepper, and 3g of thyme until the batter is smooth.
Melt 20g of butter in a small pan over medium-high heat.
Sauté banana coins for 2 minutes per side until deeply caramelized.
Remove hot skillets from the oven and divide remaining 40g of butter between them.
Pour batter equally into the hot skillets immediately.
Arrange the sautéed banana coins on top of the batter in each skillet.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the edges are high, puffed, and golden brown.
Simmer raspberries and red wine vinegar in a small saucepan for 6 minutes.
Strain the raspberry mixture through a fine-mesh sieve to create a smooth gastrique.
Drizzle the warm gastrique over each Dutch baby.
Garnish with the remaining 2g of fresh thyme.
notes: Ensure the skillets are smoking hot before adding batter for maximum lift.
The gastrique should be tangy to balance the natural sweetness of the bananas.
Do not open the oven door during the first 10 minutes of baking.

recipes.recipe_name: Arugula and Potato Cream Soup
recipes.visual_description: This vibrant, deep emerald green soup is presented in a wide-rimmed, polished white porcelain bowl. The liquid has a perfectly smooth, velvety texture. At the center, a cluster of whole toasted golden-brown pine nuts sits alongside three thin, translucent shavings of Parmigiano Reggiano. A precise drizzle of bright yellow extra virgin olive oil forms a broken ring around the central garnish. The dish is set on a light oak bistro table. A crisp, folded white cotton napkin and a heavy silver soup spoon are placed neatly to the right. Natural side-lighting highlights the matte surface of the soup and the glossy oil droplets. The composition is clean, centered, and highlights the intense natural color of the pureed arugula.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty focaccia or ciabatta
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine like Vermentino
Present as a 'primo piatto' (first course)
instructions: Clean and slice the leek.
Peel potatoes and cut into 2cm cubes.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté leeks for 5 minutes until soft.
Add potato cubes and stir to coat.
Pour in vegetable stock.
Bring to a boil then reduce heat.
Simmer for 15 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Add the arugula to the pot.
Simmer for 1 minute until wilted.
Blend the soup until completely smooth using an immersion blender.
Whisk in heavy cream and grated Parmigiano Reggiano.
Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Toast pine nuts in a small dry pan until golden.
Ladle into bowls and serve immediately.
notes: Do not overcook the arugula to maintain the bright green color.
Use a high-speed blender for the smoothest restaurant-quality texture.
Ensure the potatoes are fully soft before blending to avoid graininess.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Braised Chicken with Tomato and Olives
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown seared bone-in chicken thigh is centered on a wide, matte white porcelain plate. The chicken is nestled in a rich, creamy pale-orange sauce made from yogurt and tomatoes. Thick chunks of softened green apples and whole dark purple Kalamata olives are scattered around the meat. Small, irregular crumbles of white feta cheese provide a bright contrast against the savory sauce. The chicken skin is crisp and glistening with lemon zest. Beside the plate sits a small bowl of crusty bread and a silver fork. The setting is a rustic wooden bistro table with a folded white linen napkin. Lighting is soft, natural, and directional, highlighting the textures of the braised fruit and poultry.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita or crusty sourdough bread
Pair with a crisp dry white wine
Present in a shallow ceramic bowl
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt, pepper, and oregano.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 2 minutes. Remove from pan.
Sauté diced apples and garlic in the same pan for 3 minutes.
Add tomatoes and olives. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Return chicken to the pan. Cover and simmer until chicken reaches 75°C.
Whisk yogurt, egg, and lemon juice in a small bowl.
Stir 2 tablespoons of hot braising liquid into the yogurt mixture to temper.
Remove pan from heat. Gently stir in yogurt mixture and feta cheese.
Top with lemon zest before serving.
notes: Temper the yogurt mixture slowly to prevent curdling
Ensure the pan is off the heat when adding the egg-yogurt sauce
Use tart apples to balance the richness of the cheese

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Pork Belly with Daikon Radish
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised pork belly and daikon radish served in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl. The dish features four large, 3cm cubes of pork belly with a glossy, dark mahogany glaze. Beside the pork, three large, irregular wedges of daikon radish appear translucent, stained by the dark soy sauce. The sauce is thick and syrupy, pooling at the bottom of the bowl. Fresh, bright green scallion threads are piled neatly on top. The bowl sits on a light oak table. A small side bowl of steamed white rice and dark wood chopsticks are placed to the right. Natural side lighting highlights the gelatinous texture of the pork fat and the moist surface of the radish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice to balance the rich sauce
Accompany with a side of quick-pickled cucumbers
Present with hot Oolong tea to cleanse the palate

ingredients.name: Daikon radish, peeled and cut into large wedges

instructions: Place pork cubes in a pot of cold water. Bring to a boil for 3 minutes. Drain and rinse pork under cold water.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Add rock sugar. Stir until melted and amber-colored.
Add blanched pork to the pot. Stir to coat the meat in the caramelized sugar.
Add ginger slices and scallion lengths. Fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Deglaze the pot with Shaoxing wine. Add dark soy sauce and light soy sauce.
Pour in water or stock. Add star anise and cinnamon stick.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add radish wedges. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes until radish is tender.
Remove lid. Increase heat to medium-high. Reduce sauce for 10 minutes until thick and glossy.
Discard ginger, scallions, and whole spices before serving.
notes: Ensure the sugar does not burn when caramelizing to avoid bitterness
The radish should be fork-tender but not falling apart
Dark soy sauce is essential for the deep mahogany color of the pork

recipes.recipe_name: Mortadella and Pistachio Kofta in Smoked Makhani Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish features three golden-brown, seared mortadella kofta spheres arranged in an organic, flowing line across a matte charcoal-grey designer plate. A vibrant, silky-smooth orange makhani sauce is poured around the base, allowed to spread naturally with significant negative space. Each sphere is topped with a single, paper-thin flake of edible silver leaf and a dusting of vibrant green pistachio powder. Two delicate micro-coriander leaves provide a vertical accent. The setting is a dark travertine table with a polished brass spoon and a hand-woven white linen napkin. Dramatic side lighting highlights the glossy texture of the sauce and the subtle char on the mortadella spheres.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with garlic-infused sourdough naan
Accompany with aged basmati rice pilaf
Include a side of pickled red onions
instructions: Pulse mortadella in a food processor to a fine paste.
Fold in crushed pistachios and 2g garam masala.
Form into 12 uniform spheres.
Chill spheres for 20 minutes.
Heat oil in a heavy pan.
Sear spheres until golden on all sides.
Simmer tomato puree with ginger-garlic paste for 15 minutes.
Whisk in butter and cream until silky.
Add remaining garam masala, cardamom, and fenugreek.
Strain sauce through a fine chinois.
Warm spheres in the sauce for 2 minutes.
notes: Ensure mortadella is cold when processing to maintain emulsion
Use a smoking gun for the sauce to achieve a traditional dhungar flavor
Strain the sauce twice for maximum silkiness

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Beef Goulash
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl on a dark oak table. The focus is a hearty portion of Hungarian beef stew. The beef is cut into 3cm chunks, appearing dark red and tender. Vibrant orange carrots are cut into 2cm rounds. Potatoes are 2cm cubes, absorbing the deep red sauce. The sauce is thick and glossy, colored intensely by sweet paprika. Red bell peppers are cut into 2cm squares. A single dollop of white sour cream is placed on the side. A sprig of fresh parsley is the garnish. A side of crusty rye bread rests on a small ceramic plate next to the bowl. Natural light creates soft shadows and highlights the rich textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Galuska or Nokedli dumplings
Accompany with pickled cucumbers or fermented cabbage
Provide thick slices of fresh rye bread for dipping
instructions: Cut beef into 3cm chunks.
Finely dice onions and mince garlic.
Cut carrots into 2cm rounds and potatoes into 2cm cubes.
Dice tomatoes and cut bell pepper into 2cm squares.
Heat lard in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Sauté onions until translucent and golden.
Remove pot from heat and stir in paprika and caraway seeds.
Add beef chunks and return to heat.
Sear meat for 5 minutes until browned.
Add garlic, tomatoes, and bell pepper.
Pour in beef stock and add bay leaf.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 90 minutes.
Add potatoes and carrots.
Simmer for 30 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
notes: Do not boil the paprika over high heat to avoid bitterness.
The stew is even better when reheated the next day.
Ensure the beef is chuck or a similar braising cut for tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom Risotto with Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of glossy mushroom risotto is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The rice has a fluid, 'all'onda' consistency, spreading naturally toward the edges with a creamy, velvety sheen. In the center, a cluster of thick, golden-brown seared porcini and cremini mushroom chunks provides a focal point. Fine snow-like shavings of Parmigiano Reggiano and bright green chopped parsley are scattered across the top. The plate is set on a dark walnut bistro table. A polished silver spoon and a grey cotton napkin are placed neatly to the side. Natural, soft window lighting highlights the texture of the rice grains and the caramelized edges of the mushrooms, creating a clean, professional restaurant presentation with ample negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while the rice maintains its fluid texture.
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine like Gavi or Pinot Grigio.
Provide a small bowl of extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
instructions: Heat stock in a pot and maintain a low simmer.
Clean mushrooms and cut into 5mm thick chunks.
Sauté mushrooms in a large pan with oil over high heat until browned.
Season mushrooms with salt and set aside.
Melt 20g butter in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add shallots and sauté until translucent.
Add rice to the pot. Toast for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until the liquid evaporates.
Add one ladle of hot stock. Stir constantly.
Add more stock only after the previous ladle is absorbed.
Continue process for 18 minutes until rice is al dente.
Remove pot from heat.
Add remaining cold butter and grated Parmesan.
Stir vigorously for 1 minute to create a creamy emulsion.
Fold in three-quarters of the sautéed mushrooms.
Adjust consistency with a splash of stock. The risotto must flow.
Garnish with remaining mushroom chunks and parsley.
notes: Use cold butter at the end to ensure a better emulsion.
Constant stirring is essential to release the rice starch for creaminess.
Do not overcook the rice; it should have a slight bite in the center.

recipes.recipe_name: Miso-Glazed Acorn Squash Canapés
recipes.visual_description: Twelve 3cm cubes of miso-glazed acorn squash are arranged on a dark, textured slate platter. The squash cubes exhibit a deep golden-orange color with caramelized edges from roasting. Each cube is topped with a delicate, translucent curl of its own dark green fermented skin, providing a textural contrast. A small cluster of toasted, ivory-colored squash seeds is perched atop the skin ribbons. The arrangement is clean and minimalist, utilizing negative space on the slate. Soft, directional natural light highlights the glossy miso glaze and the matte texture of the stone. A single sprig of fresh shiso or a small radish sprout adds a touch of green. The presentation honors the Japanese philosophy of Mottainai by utilizing every part of the vegetable.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on a dark stone slab or handcrafted ceramic plate
Provide small bamboo picks for guests
Accompany with hot green tea or chilled sake
instructions: Wash squash thoroughly to clean the skin.
Halve the squash and scoop out the seeds.
Rinse seeds, pat dry, and toast in a dry pan until golden.
Peel the squash with a vegetable peeler to create thin ribbons of skin.
Massage skin ribbons with rice vinegar, salt, and sugar. Let sit for 20 minutes.
Cut the squash flesh into uniform 3cm cubes.
Whisk miso, mirin, soy sauce, and sesame oil in a bowl.
Toss squash cubes in the miso mixture until coated.
Roast cubes at 200°C for 20 minutes until tender and caramelized.
Place one roasted squash cube on a serving platter.
Top each cube with a curled ribbon of the fermented skin.
Garnish with a cluster of toasted squash seeds.
notes: Ensure the squash skin is sliced very thin for the best pickling texture
The seeds provide a necessary nutty crunch to balance the soft roasted flesh
Use any leftover miso marinade as a dressing for steamed greens

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Kiev
recipes.visual_description: The centerpiece is a single, golden-brown Chicken Kiev, presented as a whole, plump oval. The exterior shows a crunchy, uniform panko texture with a deep amber color. It rests on a smooth mound of creamy, white mashed potatoes. Three whole roasted baby carrots with green tops intact lie alongside the chicken. A light drizzle of herb butter pools naturally at the base of the chicken. The dish is served on a clean white porcelain plate with significant negative space. The setting is a modern bistro with a light wood table. A white cotton napkin and polished silver flatware are placed to the right. Natural light emphasizes the crisp breading. The chicken remains whole and unsliced.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Mizeria, a traditional Polish cucumber salad with sour cream and dill.
Garnish with a large sprig of fresh dill.
Accompany with a side of buttered green peas.
instructions: Mix softened butter with minced garlic, parsley, and lemon juice.
Form butter into four small cylinders.
Freeze butter logs for 20 minutes until firm.
Pound chicken breasts to 5mm thickness between plastic wrap sheets.
Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Place one frozen butter log in the center of each chicken breast.
Fold chicken tightly around the butter to create a sealed oval.
Dredge chicken in flour, then dip in beaten eggs.
Coat thoroughly in panko breadcrumbs.
Refrigerate breaded chicken for 30 minutes to set.
Heat oil to 170°C in a deep pan.
Fry chicken for 4 minutes until golden brown.
Transfer chicken to a baking tray.
Bake at 180°C until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
notes: Ensure the chicken is rolled tightly to prevent the butter from leaking during cooking.
Double-coating in egg and breadcrumbs can provide a more secure seal.
Use high-fat European-style butter for a richer flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Basque-Style Chicken with Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Basque-Style Chicken served in a wide white porcelain bowl. Two whole bone-in chicken thighs show crispy, seared golden-brown skin. The chicken sits on a thick piperade sauce of long, softened red and green bell pepper strips and translucent sliced onions. The sauce is a rich, matte red from simmered tomatoes. Natural light highlights the moist texture of the vegetables and the rendered fat on the poultry skin. Bright green chopped parsley is scattered across the dish. A side of thick-cut crusty baguette rests on a small wooden board next to the bowl. The background is a clean, dark wood bistro table with a linen napkin and a silver fork.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette to soak up the sauce
Pair with a crisp white wine from the Irouléguy region
Traditional accompaniment of steamed white rice

ingredients.name: Red bell peppers, sliced into 1cm strips
Green bell peppers, sliced into 1cm strips

instructions: Season chicken with salt and Piment d'Espelette.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Sauté onions and bell peppers in the same pan for 8 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in white wine and scrape the pan bottom to deglaze.
Add crushed tomatoes and chicken stock.
Return chicken to the pan, keeping skin above the liquid.
Simmer covered over medium-low heat for 25 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Garnish with chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Maintain a gentle simmer to keep the chicken moist
Piment d'Espelette provides the characteristic mild heat of the Basque region

recipes.recipe_name: Sichuan Pork and Cucumber Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a wide, shallow celadon ceramic bowl centered on a dark wood bistro table. The primary focus is the contrast between the vibrant, jade-green cucumber batons and the deeply seared, golden-brown pork cubes. The cucumbers retain a slight translucency from the quick wok-sear. The pork is arranged in rustic, bite-sized chunks, never sliced or fanned. Glossy dark sauce coats every element, reflecting light. Small flecks of toasted Sichuan peppercorns and bright red dried chili sections are scattered throughout. A garnish of thinly sliced green scallions adds a fresh vertical element. Beside the bowl, a pair of dark wood chopsticks rests on a small porcelain holder. The lighting is natural and even.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice in a separate small porcelain bowl
Accompany with a side of smashed cucumber salad for texture contrast
Provide high-quality oolong tea to cleanse the palate
instructions: Mix pork cubes with 15ml soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch.
Marinate pork for 15 minutes.
Toss cucumber batons with 5g salt in a bowl.
Let cucumbers sit for 10 minutes.
Rinse cucumbers under cold water and pat thoroughly dry.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add pork cubes in a single layer.
Sear pork until golden brown on all sides.
Verify pork internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove pork from wok and set aside.
Add garlic, ginger, chilis, and peppercorns to the remaining oil.
Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add dried cucumbers to the wok.
Stir-fry on high heat for 2 minutes.
Return pork to the wok.
Add remaining soy sauce and sesame oil.
Toss rapidly for 1 minute to glaze.
Serve immediately.
notes: Salting the cucumbers is essential to maintain a crisp texture during high-heat cooking.
Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding ingredients to achieve authentic wok hei aroma.
Adjust the number of dried chilis to control the heat level.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan-Style Creamy Sun-dried Tomato Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single, whole pan-seared chicken breast sits centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken features a deep golden-brown crust. It is partially submerged in a rich, vibrant orange-red cream sauce. Thin julienne strips of dark red sun-dried tomatoes and bright green wilted spinach leaves are scattered through the sauce. The plate has a moderate amount of negative space. A few small, fresh basil leaves are placed on top for garnish. The setting is a modern bistro with a light wooden table. Natural light highlights the glossy texture of the sauce and the rustic sear on the meat. A cotton napkin and a polished silver fork lie beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread to soak up the sauce
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine like Gavi or Pinot Grigio
Present on a pre-warmed porcelain plate
instructions: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken for 6-7 minutes per side until golden brown.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add diced shallots to the same skillet and sauté for 2 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and julienned sun-dried tomatoes for 1 minute.
Deglaze the pan with chicken stock, scraping up browned bits.
Pour in heavy cream and bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in grated parmesan until the sauce thickens and emulsifies.
Add baby spinach and red pepper flakes, stirring until spinach wilts.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet to coat in sauce.
Garnish with fresh basil before serving.
notes: Use the oil from the sun-dried tomato jar for extra flavor when searing the chicken
Do not boil the cream rapidly to prevent splitting
Freshly grated parmesan provides a smoother sauce consistency than pre-shredded cheese

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Squid with Citrus Bell Pepper Glaze and Avocado
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a clean white porcelain plate. The focal point is a pile of golden-brown seared squid chunks and 2cm rustic torn pieces of fried bread. A vibrant red bell pepper reduction coats the squid, glistening under natural light. To the side, neat 1cm cubes of green avocado are arranged with a salsa of 5mm diced pale green apple, orange cantaloupe, and bright green kiwi. Quartered purple grapes provide a color contrast. The dish is set on a light wood bistro table with a white cotton napkin and silver fork. The lighting is soft and even, highlighting the textures of the tender squid and crisp bread.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a warm ensalada with chilled white wine.
Accompany with extra lime wedges for acidity.
instructions: Dice bell pepper into 5mm pieces.
Dice apple, melon, and kiwi into 5mm cubes.
Quarter the grapes.
Dice avocado into 1cm cubes.
Whisk orange juice, lime juice, crushed raspberries, and sugar in a small saucepan.
Add diced bell peppers to the saucepan.
Simmer mixture over medium heat until liquid reduces by half.
Pat squid dry and cut into 3cm chunks.
Heat olive oil in a heavy skillet over high heat.
Season squid with salt and pepper.
Sear squid chunks for 90 seconds until opaque.
Toss torn fried bread chunks into the pan to warm.
Combine apple, melon, kiwi, and grapes in a small bowl.
Plate squid and bread immediately.
Drizzle with bell pepper reduction and garnish with avocado cubes and fruit salsa.
notes: Ensure the pan is smoking hot before adding squid to prevent steaming.
The sugar in the glaze helps achieve a deep caramelization on the bell peppers.

recipes.recipe_name: Bergamot and Butterscotch Glazed Pork Belly
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick block of slow-braised pork belly sits centrally on a smooth bed of ivory-white parsnip puree. The pork skin is deeply caramelized and coated in a glossy, translucent amber glaze made from bergamot and butterscotch. Small, golden-brown crispy bacon lardons are scattered naturally around the base of the meat. Tiny flecks of bright green bergamot zest and a single fresh thyme sprig provide vibrant color accents. The dish is presented on a minimalist matte grey stoneware plate, showing the entire composition with balanced negative space. Soft side lighting emphasizes the crackled texture of the pork skin and the velvety surface of the sauce. The background features a rustic oak table.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of chilled dry Riesling to cut through the richness.
Accompany with a side of bitter greens like radicchio or endive.
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C.
Score the pork belly skin in a small diamond pattern.
Season all sides with salt and pepper.
Place pork skin-side down in a cold pan.
Turn heat to medium and render fat until skin is crisp and brown.
Remove pork and set aside.
Sauté shallots, garlic, and thyme in the pork fat for 2 minutes.
Deglaze with half of the bergamot juice.
Add chicken stock and bring to a simmer.
Place pork in a baking dish with the liquid, keeping the skin above the surface.
Braise in the oven for 2.5 hours.
Boil parsnips in salted water until very soft.
Drain parsnips and blend with cream and butter until silky.
Fry bacon pieces in a separate pan until crispy.
Drain bacon on paper towels.
Remove pork from oven and strain the braising liquid into a saucepan.
Add butterscotch and remaining bergamot juice to the liquid.
Simmer over high heat until reduced to a thick, glossy glaze.
Brush glaze onto the pork and roast at 220°C for 10 minutes.
Spoon parsnip puree onto a plate.
Place the whole pork block on top.
Garnish with crispy bacon and bergamot zest.
notes: Ensure the braising liquid does not touch the scored skin to maintain crispness.
Use a fine-mesh sieve for the parsnip puree to achieve restaurant-quality texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash
recipes.visual_description: A wide white porcelain plate holds two whole bone-in chicken thighs smothered in a deep crimson, glossy paprika sauce. The sauce is thick and velvety, showing small bits of softened onion and bell pepper. To the side, a generous portion of 2 cm sautéed potato cubes displays a vibrant golden-brown crust and tender interior. A small, elegant swirl of white sour cream cuts through the red sauce, adding visual contrast. The plating is clean with moderate negative space. A single sprig of fresh parsley provides a green accent. The scene is set on a light oak table with a linen napkin and a stainless steel fork, captured in bright, natural morning light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Uborkasaláta (Hungarian cucumber salad with vinegar and garlic).
Provide a large spoon to enjoy the abundant paprika sauce.
Accompany with a glass of dry Hungarian white wine like Furmint.
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt.
Heat lard in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken on both sides until skin is golden. Remove and set aside.
Add onions to the pot. Sauté until translucent and soft.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in paprika to avoid burning.
Add diced bell pepper and tomato. Return chicken to the pot.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 35-40 minutes until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Boil potato cubes in salted water for 8-10 minutes. Drain well.
Sauté potatoes in a separate pan with oil until edges are golden and crisp.
Whisk flour into the sour cream until smooth.
Temper the sour cream by stirring in 100 ml of the hot braising liquid.
Pour the tempered mixture back into the pot. Stir constantly.
Simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens and becomes glossy.
notes: Use high-quality Hungarian sweet paprika for the most authentic flavor and color.
Never add paprika to a boiling pot or direct high heat, as it will turn bitter.
The sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Sour Curry with Agati Flowers and Prawns
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a deep ceramic Thai serving bowl filled with a vibrant orange-red broth. The hero agati flowers, with their distinct curved white petals and pale green stems, are gently submerged, appearing tender yet intact. Large whole pink prawns are nestled among the flowers, their tails curving naturally. Translucent circular white radish slices peek through the surface. The bowl is placed on a dark teak wood surface next to a small separate bowl of fluffy white jasmine rice. A traditional flat-bottomed Thai soup spoon and a stainless steel fork rest on a folded cream linen napkin. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the steam rising from the savory broth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Pair with a Thai-style omelet (Khai Jiao)
Use a traditional flat-bottomed soup spoon
instructions: Remove bitter stamens from agati flowers.
Boil shrimp stock in a large pot.
Whisk in sour curry paste until dissolved.
Add radish rounds.
Simmer 5 minutes until translucent.
Stir in tamarind, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Add whole prawns.
Cook 2 minutes until opaque.
Fold in agati flowers.
Simmer 30 seconds.
Remove from heat immediately.
notes: Always remove the stamens from agati flowers to prevent excessive bitterness.
The broth should taste primarily sour, followed by salty and slightly sweet.

recipes.recipe_name: Coffee-Rubbed Milk Tofu with Hazelnut Cookie Butter Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick rectangular block of coffee-rubbed milk tofu sits as the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain plate. The tofu has a dark, textured espresso crust from searing. A glossy, tan-colored cookie butter sauce is pooled neatly around the base of the tofu. The sauce is garnished with toasted hazelnut halves and a sprinkle of micro-herbs for contrast. The arrangement is balanced with significant negative space on the plate. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak wood table and a linen napkin. Lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the matte texture of the coffee rub against the silky sheen of the reduction sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of bitter green salad to balance the rich sauce.
Use a modern heavy-rimmed ceramic bowl for a rustic-contemporary feel.

ingredients.name: Milk tofu (Paneer), cut into 4cm thick blocks

instructions: Pat the milk tofu blocks dry with paper towels.
Mix ground coffee, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Press the coffee mixture onto the surface of the tofu blocks.
Heat oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear tofu for 3 minutes per side until a dark crust forms.
Remove tofu and keep warm.
In the same skillet, sauté shallots and garlic until translucent.
Deglaze the pan with vegetable stock, scraping up browned bits.
Whisk in the cookie butter until the sauce is smooth and glossy.
Simmer for 4 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Season the sauce with salt to balance the sweetness.
Return tofu to the pan briefly to coat in sauce.
notes: Ensure the tofu is very dry before applying the coffee rub to prevent clumping.
Adjust salt levels in the sauce carefully to counteract the sugar in the cookie butter.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Bluefish with Bacon and Alfredo Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A whole pan-seared bluefish fillet sits prominently atop a neat mound of sautéed dark green baby spinach. The fish skin is exceptionally crisp and golden-brown, contrasting with the pale, flaky meat. A velvety, ivory-white alfredo sauce is poured in a clean circle around the base of the spinach. Small, uniform cubes of deep-red crispy bacon and vibrant green chopped parsley are scattered precisely over the sauce and fish. The dish is served on a wide, white porcelain plate with significant negative space. The setting is a light wood bistro table with a white cotton napkin and polished silverware. Natural light emphasizes the glossy sauce and the texture of the seared skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp dry white wine
Accompany with a side of crusty sourdough bread
instructions: Pat bluefish fillets dry with paper towels.
Season fillets with salt and black pepper.
Dice bacon into small cubes.
Fry bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy.
Remove bacon and set aside on paper towels.
Retain 15ml of bacon fat in the skillet and add olive oil.
Place bluefish skin-side down in the skillet.
Sear for 4 minutes until skin is crisp.
Flip fillets and cook for 2 more minutes.
Remove fish and keep warm.
Sauté minced garlic and spinach in the same pan until wilted.
Heat alfredo sauce in a small saucepan.
Whisk lemon juice and half of the crispy bacon into the sauce.
Place a portion of spinach in the center of each plate.
Top spinach with one whole bluefish fillet.
Spoon sauce around the fish and garnish with remaining bacon and chopped parsley.
notes: Bluefish is an oily fish; the lemon juice in the sauce helps balance the richness.
Ensure the pan is very hot before adding the fish to achieve a crispy skin.

recipes.recipe_name: Clarified Pizza Sauce Sphere with Buffalo Mozzarella Mousse
recipes.visual_description: A single, translucent amber tomato sphere rests precisely atop a velvety mound of snow-white buffalo mozzarella mousse. The sphere’s surface is taut and glossy, containing liquid clarified pizza sauce. Vibrant, emerald-green basil oil is dotted around the base in a fluid, organic pattern. A singular, ultra-thin toasted sourdough baton leans delicately against the mousse for height. The dish is presented on a wide, matte-charcoal ceramic plate, emphasizing vast negative space and architectural elegance. The setting features a polished white Carrara marble surface with a minimalist silver tasting spoon. Soft, directional lighting creates gentle highlights on the sphere and deep, purposeful shadows, highlighting the contrast between the airy mousse and the liquid core.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a chilled amuse-bouche
Pair with a dry Franciacorta sparkling wine
Present on chilled designer stoneware
instructions: Line a fine-mesh sieve with a coffee filter.
Pour pizza sauce into the filter and drip for 4 hours.
Collect 200 ml of clarified tomato water.
Whisk calcium lactate into the tomato water.
Pour mixture into small silicone sphere molds and freeze.
Blend sodium alginate with distilled water until dissolved.
Rest the alginate bath for 1 hour to remove bubbles.
Drop frozen spheres into the alginate bath for 3 minutes.
Transfer spheres to a bowl of clean water to rinse.
Blend mozzarella, cream, and salt until completely smooth.
Pass the mixture through a fine chinois sieve.
Blanch basil leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds.
Shock basil in ice water immediately.
Blend basil with grapeseed oil on high speed.
Strain oil through a coffee filter.
Pipe a small mound of mozzarella mousse onto the center of a chilled plate.
Place one tomato sphere carefully on top of the mousse.
Drizzle three drops of basil oil around the base.
Garnish with two micro-basil leaves using tweezers.
notes: Use high-quality pizza sauce with low acidity for better clarification.
Distilled water is essential for the alginate bath to prevent premature gelling.
Ensure the mozzarella is at room temperature before blending to prevent graininess.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Chorizo and Bay Leaf
recipes.visual_description: A wide white porcelain plate features a vibrant, level bed of golden-orange Bomba rice. Large 2cm chunks of seared, deep red chorizo are distributed naturally across the surface, showing dark caramelized edges. Small 1cm dice of softened red bell pepper and bright green peas provide colorful accents throughout the rice. Two whole bay leaves are nestled among the grains. The rice is moist and glistening with a light sheen of paprika-infused oil. A single fresh lemon wedge sits on the side of the plate. The dish is presented on a light oak table with a white linen napkin and a simple silver fork. Natural side lighting emphasizes the individual rice grains and the rustic texture of the sausage.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the pan for a communal feel
Accompany with a simple green salad and crusty bread
Offer a side of alioli for extra richness
instructions: Cut chorizo into 2cm thick chunks.
Finely dice the onion and red bell pepper into 1cm pieces.
Mince the garlic cloves.
Heat olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium heat.
Sear chorizo chunks for 4 minutes until fat renders and edges are crisp.
Remove chorizo and set aside.
Add onion and red pepper to the pan fat.
Sauté for 6 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, bay leaves, and smoked paprika for 1 minute.
Add Bomba rice and stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in hot chicken stock and season with salt.
Simmer on medium-low heat for 15 minutes without stirring.
Scatter peas and seared chorizo chunks over the rice.
Cook for 5 more minutes until liquid is fully absorbed.
Remove from heat and cover with a cloth for 5 minutes.
Garnish with chopped parsley and lemon wedges.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to ensure proper texture.
Use a wide pan to allow the rice to cook evenly in a thin layer.
The resting period is essential for the rice to finish absorbing moisture.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Paprika and Lemon Pasta with Pan-Seared Cheese
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pasta is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The fusilli pasta is coated in a pale, creamy orange-tinted sauce flecked with bright green herbs. Large, 2-centimeter cubes of golden-brown seared cheese are placed naturally on top of the pasta, showing distinct caramelized edges. Finely diced green pickles and vibrant chopped parsley are scattered throughout the dish. A light dusting of red paprika and fresh lemon zest provides a color contrast. The bowl sits on a dark oak bistro table with a folded white linen napkin and a heavy silver fork. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the glossy sauce and the matte texture of the seared cheese.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty rye bread
Accompany with a crisp pilsner or dry white wine

ingredients.name: Grilling cheese (Halloumi or firm white cheese)

instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water.
Cook pasta until al dente.
Reserve 100 ml of pasta cooking water.
Drain pasta.
Finely dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Sauté onion in 15 ml olive oil over medium heat until translucent.
Add garlic and paprika. Cook for 1 minute.
Whisk mayonnaise, lemon juice, and reserved pasta water in a small bowl.
Cut cheese into 2 cm thick cubes.
Sear cheese cubes in remaining olive oil over high heat until golden on all sides.
Finely dice the pickled cucumber.
Toss warm pasta with onion mixture and lemon-mayonnaise sauce.
Fold in diced pickles, chopped parsley, and torn basil.
Season with black pepper.
Top with the whole seared cheese cubes.
notes: Do not boil the mayonnaise sauce; toss it with warm pasta off the heat to prevent splitting.
Ensure the cheese is patted dry before searing to achieve a crisp crust.

recipes.recipe_name: Cultured Milk Mousse with Dill and Brown Butter
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of cultured milk mousse is presented in a shallow, handcrafted matte cream ceramic bowl. The mousse forms a smooth, ivory-colored base with a silky texture. A small, concentrated pool of vibrant red lingonberry jam is placed off-center. Beside the jam, a neat cluster of golden-brown oat and brown butter crumble adds a rustic, toasted element. Precise droplets of bright green dill oil are dispersed across the surface, creating a striking visual contrast against the white cream. The entire bowl is captured on a textured, reclaimed light wood surface under soft, natural morning light. An undyed linen napkin and a single silver dessert spoon complete the minimalist, eco-conscious Nordic presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in traditional stoneware or ceramic vessels
Pair with a glass of chilled birch sap or herbal tea
Present as a refreshing conclusion to a seasonal forage-focused meal
instructions: Combine milk, cream, and buttermilk in a glass jar.
Cover with a breathable cloth.
Ferment at room temperature for 24 hours until thickened.
Bloom gelatin in cold water for 5 minutes.
Warm 50ml of the fermented mixture with honey over low heat.
Stir in squeezed gelatin until dissolved.
Whisk gelatin mixture back into the remaining cold fermented cream.
Pour into 4 individual ceramic bowls.
Refrigerate for 4 hours until set.
Melt butter in a small pan over medium heat.
Cook until the milk solids turn golden brown and smell nutty.
Add ground oats to the pan.
Toast oats in the brown butter until crisp and fragrant.
Remove from heat and cool completely.
Blanch dill in boiling water for 10 seconds.
Shock in ice water and pat dry.
Blend dill with 30ml neutral oil until smooth.
Strain through a coffee filter to obtain clear green oil.
Spoon a small amount of jam onto each set mousse.
Top with the brown butter oat crumble.
Drizzle with dill oil before serving.
notes: Use high-quality local butter for the best Maillard reaction flavor.
The dill oil can be made using leftover dill stems to ensure zero waste.
If lingonberry jam is unavailable, use any tart, wild berry preserve.

recipes.recipe_name: Argentinian Grilled Beef with Chimichurri and Roasted Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single 200g whole beef striploin steak sits prominently on a matte white ceramic plate, featuring a deep mahogany crust and distinct char marks. The steak is presented whole, never sliced. A vibrant, herbaceous green chimichurri sauce is spooned over the center, showing visible bits of minced garlic and chopped parsley. To the side, a rustic pile of roasted red bell pepper strips and charred red onion wedges adds deep crimson and purple tones. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark oak table. A linen napkin and a simple steak knife are placed beside the plate. Natural side lighting emphasizes the glistening surface of the meat and the glossy texture of the roasted vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of Malbec
Accompany with warm crusty bread
Provide extra chimichurri in a small terracotta bowl

ingredients.name: Beef striploin (Bife de Chorizo), cut into 4 thick steaks
Sea salt and cracked black pepper

instructions: Finely chop the parsley and combine with minced garlic in a bowl.
Whisk in the dried oregano, chili flakes, red wine vinegar, and 100ml of olive oil.
Season the chimichurri with salt and let it rest for at least 30 minutes.
Char the whole bell peppers over an open flame or under a broiler until the skin is black.
Place charred peppers in a bowl and cover with plastic wrap for 10 minutes to steam.
Peel the peppers, remove seeds, and cut into 2cm thick strips.
Slice the red onion into 1cm thick wedges and sauté in remaining oil until tender and charred.
Toss the pepper strips with the onions and season with salt.
Season the beef steaks generously with salt on all sides.
Sear the steaks in a hot cast-iron skillet for 4 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Rest the whole steaks for 5 minutes before serving.
Top each steak with a generous spoonful of chimichurri.
notes: Ensure the steak is at room temperature before cooking
The chimichurri flavor improves if made several hours in advance
Use a very hot pan to achieve the traditional crust

recipes.recipe_name: Massaman-Style Yam and Sweet Potato Curry
recipes.visual_description: A deep ceramic bowl contains a vibrant Massaman curry with a glossy, golden-brown coconut sauce. The dish features 3cm cubes of roasted yam and orange sweet potato. Whole peeled shallots and a cinnamon stick rest among the vegetables. The sauce has a rich, fluid consistency. Coarsely crushed toasted almonds and fresh Thai basil leaves are scattered across the top. The bowl sits on a rustic wooden table. A side bowl of steamed jasmine rice and a ceramic Thai spoon accompany the meal. The lighting is bright and natural. The arrangement is organic and clean. The entire plate is visible against a minimal bistro background. The colors are warm and inviting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Accompany with Thai cucumber relish (Ajat)
Use a traditional ceramic Thai spoon and fork
instructions: Peel yam and sweet potato.
Cut tubers into 3cm cubes.
Heat coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Fry curry paste for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in coconut milk and vegetable stock.
Stir in maple syrup, tamarind paste, and soy sauce.
Add yam, sweet potato, whole shallots, star anise, and cinnamon.
Simmer for 25 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Toast almonds in a dry pan until golden.
Crush almonds into coarse pieces.
Garnish curry with almonds and fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure the curry paste is shrimp-paste free for a strictly plant-based version.
Do not overcook the tubers to maintain distinct cube shapes.

recipes.recipe_name: Argentinian Grilled Beef with Chimichurri and Roasted Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single 200g whole beef striploin steak sits prominently on a matte white ceramic plate, featuring a deep mahogany crust and distinct char marks. The steak is presented whole, never sliced. A vibrant, herbaceous green chimichurri sauce is spooned over the center, showing visible bits of minced garlic and chopped parsley. To the side, a rustic pile of roasted red bell pepper strips and charred red onion wedges adds deep crimson and purple tones. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark oak table. A linen napkin and a simple steak knife are placed beside the plate. Natural side lighting emphasizes the glistening surface of the meat and the glossy texture of the roasted vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of Malbec
Accompany with warm crusty bread
Provide extra chimichurri in a small terracotta bowl

ingredients.name: Beef striploin (Bife de Chorizo), cut into 4 thick steaks
Sea salt and cracked black pepper

instructions: Finely chop the parsley and combine with minced garlic in a bowl.
Whisk in the dried oregano, chili flakes, red wine vinegar, and 100ml of olive oil.
Season the chimichurri with salt and let it rest for at least 30 minutes.
Char the whole bell peppers over an open flame or under a broiler until the skin is black.
Place charred peppers in a bowl and cover with plastic wrap for 10 minutes to steam.
Peel the peppers, remove seeds, and cut into 2cm thick strips.
Slice the red onion into 1cm thick wedges and sauté in remaining oil until tender and charred.
Toss the pepper strips with the onions and season with salt.
